“As for myself, I believe that what will always remain in the hearts of everyone is change,” she said, her tone resolute. “Changes in everyday life, changes in those around us, and changes within ourselves. For uneventful and flat routines do not leave impressions within the heart. This… is something that I believe all of you have just realized for yourselves.”
Her words elicited a chorus of nods throughout the audience, clearly in agreement. Confirming that her message had taken root among the students, she continued.

“Change: that’s what’s necessary to etch the days you spend at this school more deeply into your hearts for the rest of your lives. Change—significant change—is what I will bring about to this school if elected student council president, and it will begin with listening to all of your voices. Not sweeping reforms or radical transformations, but changes that will add color and a little enjoyment to all your daily lives. As a first step toward this ideal, I will be holding a brand-new event today at 4:30 p.m. Something that this school has never had before: a Christmas party.”
By this point, the audience was completely captivated by her speech.

“I am sure that some of you are eager to head home to enjoy the winter break to its fullest, while others have already made plans to go out and have fun with friends,” Yuki smiled, continuing to address the students. “But please consider this. Today’s the only day you can attend a Christmas party at this school, you know? The time you’ll spend relaxing at home, the time you’ll spend hanging out with all your friends: both will be enjoyable, sure, but which do you think you will still remember a year from now?”

The answer to such a question had naturally already sprouted within the hearts of those who were listening. Looking out at the wave of students, who were clearly deeply moved, Yuki delivered her final push.
“So, everyone, I am sincerely asking you to join the Christmas party that I am hosting. Because if you do, I am sure that all my beliefs—my ideals—will be conveyed to you all as well.”
Her words conveyed nothing but an appeal of utter sincerity, one finished with a radiant smile as she continued to meet the eyes within the audience.
“On that note and with this announcement, I would now like to bring my address to a close,” Yuki proclaimed in a bright voice. “Thank you all very much for your attention.”
With those final words, her speech came to its end.

She lowered her head into a bow. Silence lingered for a heartbeat, before thunderous applause erupted throughout the crowd. Accompanying whistles and cheers calling in support for her quickly enveloped the gymnasium, rising in a wave indistinguishable from a standing ovation.
Are you for real? Masachika couldn’t help but mutter in his heart. She’s reeeally good at speeches.
No, he had always known that Yuki was a good public speaker. He knew that, but….
What is this…? A ridiculous power up or something? This girl…

A growing sense of unease slowly crept throughout his chest; the excitement and sense of unity that had taken over the gymnasium far exceeded his expectations. It felt so overwhelming that his own intuition was screaming to tell him that even Alisa’s words would never reach the hearts of the audience if she were to give her speech now.
No, thank God Ayano’s still gotta go… Alya’s voice should surely reach them if the mood settles down a li’l there. Probably…
Though Masachika was fully aware that his thoughts had spiraled into wishful thinking—far from calm and calculating—he had yet to descend into a full-blown panic.
…At least, not yet.
“Thank you very much, Suou-san,” the emcee’s voice once again echoed through the gymnasium. “Next, we will hear some remarks from the student council’s secretary, Ayano Kimishima.”
Hearing her cue, Ayano turned to Yuki before stepping onto the stage. “I will be taking my turn.”
“Mm,” Yuki nodded to her quiet voice. “I’ll leave the rest to you.”
Her words were so simple, yet they carried her complete trust. Ayano could only stop in her tracks as she heard them, continuing her steps after a moment.

As for her closing ceremony speech, Yuki had never specifically instructed her to say this or talk about so and so. It had been the same during the first semester as well. Even when Ayano had asked about what she should talk about, all Yuki had done was tell her to think of it herself. It was surely a sign of the trust she had in Ayano, and at the same time… a testament to Yuki’s belief that parroting the words of someone else meant you could never truly move the hearts of those who were listening.
I have come to understand that now, Ayano reflected.

It was something she had not grasped back during the first semester, and was why all she had done was simply list Yuki’s virtues and strengths as she thought, appealing to the audience for their support. It wasn’t something she thought of as a mistake, per se… but maybe it wasn’t what was needed to move the hearts of others.
Ayano had come to terms with this fact most strongly during the student assembly last month when she had heard the pleas of the vice president of the piano club, Aoi Tsukamoto.

Listening to her appeal from the wings of the stage had allowed her to understand firsthand: rather than words meticulously woven together in one’s mind… a voice that draws from the heart in its most natural and unaltered shape could, at times, move others more deeply.
And that’s precisely why…
I will… say things as they are. About why I wish to support Yuki-sama. All of it.
Holding only that conviction in her heart, Ayano stepped onto the stage, letting her thoughts drift back to the distant past as she slowly began to speak.
“I do not think that all of you know this, but… when Yuki-sama was young, she suffered from severe asthma.”
Murmurs rippled throughout the audience at her unexpected revelation, delivered before she had even bothered to introduce herself. Paying no attention to any of it, Ayano pushed on.

“As a child, Yuki-sama’s asthma had rendered her unable to attend elementary school properly and… she spent most of each day confined to her bed. Vigorous exercise was out of the question, of course, but more than that, she could not even laugh or cry as her heart wished. Both it and her body were bound by illness.”
The initial confusion that weighed on the students gradually, yet steadily, gave way as Ayano’s words sank into their heads.

“But even so, Yuki-sama had always conducted herself as a brave girl on the surface. Even when she could not get out of bed… she spent her days cheerfully, always with a bright smile, so as to not worry her family.”
For a moment, silence settled over the room as Ayano fought past the lump in her throat.
“However, precisely because of that...”

By this point, a crack had formed in her expressionless façade with tension gathering between her brows. Her throat continued to tighten and her normally flat tone contorted as notes of pain made their way into her voice.
“Seeing Yuki-sama whenever she suffered an asthma attack was truly agonizing; truly pitiful… It made I, who could do nothing but stand by her side and watch, feel utterly helpless and heartbroken…”

The air felt drawn tight as a wire, making even those who were listening finding themselves holding their breaths. Perhaps because her throat had completely given way at this point, Ayano broke off her words, taking a long, deep breath as if to compose herself.

“And yet…” she slowly began again after resetting her expression, “even in such unbearable circumstances, Yuki-sama never turned bitter… She never turned sour and remained noble to the very end. As the heir to the Suou family, she resolved to fulfill what was expected of her. She held that oath firmly within her heart and never allowed her illness to break her spirit, working harder than anyone else. It was from watching that noble figure up close that I came to desire to stand in service to her. I truly decided that I wanted to help her with everything I had.”
Her voice, albeit still pierced with small, lingering traces of pain, carried a powerful warmth that shook the hearts of those in the audience.
Whether she was aware of its effect or not, Ayano pushed on once again, now looking straight ahead.

“After that, Yuki-sama overcame her illness and… despite bearing the tremendous handicap of having spent so many of her early years bedridden, she grew into a splendid young lady, showing no signs of such a past whatsoever. Brimming with knowledge and sophistication, she became a paragon of what a lady should be like, someone whom everyone at this school respects and admires.”
Still, this was something everyone present already knew.

“However…” Ayano paused, her voice ringing with absolute conviction, ready to share something no one else could have possibly known. “I know about it all. I know just how precious and rare her presence has truly become. That is precisely why I will continue to support Yuki-sama with all my strength. I will, without a doubt, use everything I have to support her, to assist her. That is my resolve, and the very meaning of my existence as the person known as Ayano Kimishima…”
Her words hung in the heavy silence that followed. Then, as if jolted back to the reality of her audience, Ayano quickly lowered her head in gratitude.
“Thank you very much for your kind attention.”
Stepping down from the stage, she was met with only hesitant, scattered claps… before they gradually grew louder, transforming into thunderous applause.
“Oooooohhhhhh!!!”
“We’re rooting for youuuu!!!”
“Do your beeeest!!!”
Passionate cheers roared one after another as Yuki and Ayano stood together at the right wing of the stage, their heads lowered into a bow.
There was no doubt about it whatsoever.
The stars of the moment were Yuki and Ayano.
Watching the scene unfold from the other wing of the stage, Masachika could not help but grimace at how far the audience’s excitement had exceeded his expectations.
“Wait, wait, wait, wait…” he muttered in disbelief, his sheer panic escaping from his lips.
Oh shit, oh shit. This is… seriously bad. They’ve taken complete control of the room.

To top it all off, Yuki had painted her platform not on that of sweeping reforms or major changes, but rather a multitude of small changes: a position that directly conflicted with Alisa’s own agenda. With an audience won over so clearly and early like this, just how many students would even be willing to listen to her at this point…?
Damn it, I totally underestimated them… I never imagined things would become this one-sided.

There was no other way to describe it but a blunder. He had been so focused on Yuki’s supposed hidden trump card—the Christmas party—that he had satisfied himself merely by just preparing something capable of matching just that.

But thinking about it calmly… there was no way that those two, known for preparing everything with intense and meticulous care, would have been satisfied with an ordinary speech in just announcing some party.
Tch, now ain’t that right! Why did I assume they’d only play it safe on the day of the dang closing ceremony!?
Masachika had never thought that he was letting his guard down.

And yet… without even realizing it himself, he had grown completely complacent, probably intoxicated somewhere deep down by all this sense of omnipotence that had come with this supposed “invincible mode” he was in.
Now, not even a fragment of that exhilaration remained.
Gah, I can save the regret for later! Masachika desperately racked his brain. Right now’s for figuring out how to get through this…!
But just them, a voice suddenly reached his ear.
“Are you okay, Alya-chan?” It belonged to none other than Maria.

Startled by her quiet voice, Masachika turned toward her, only to find Alisa there, standing with her usual stern expression, yet an undeniable air of unease. Beside her was Maria, looking at her with concern… The sight made Masachika want to beat himself senseless for carelessly letting his panic show.
Gah, the heck am I doing…!? I’m the one who said I’d support her…!
But while he grounded his teeth in frustration… the moment arrived.
“Up next, the student council’s treasurer, Alisa Kujou-san, will now give her address.”
The emcee’s announcement rang through the gymnasium, signalling their turn. Without saying even a word to Masachika, Alisa stepped forward with a tense expression.
…Only for Masachika to instinctively grab her hand and stop her.
“Hm!? Masachika-kun?”
Alisa turned around in surprise. Meeting her gaze, Masachika made his mind up in an instant.
“Change of plans,” he declared in a resolute tone. “I’m going up.”
“Eh? But…”
“Just wait, ’kay?” he forced on a fearless grin to his partner’s wavering gaze. “I’ll take back the atmosphere for sure.”

With the bold proclamation, Masachika strode toward the stage without waiting for a response. A chorus of confused whispers rose from both the audience and the emcee, but he had no room to care about that now.
Oh shiiit. I’ve got nothing.
The speech he’d originally prepared might as well have been a blank sheet of paper now. It was all winging it from here on.
This ain’t even funny…

And he was right. There was nothing funny about the situation at all. All Masachika could do now was bitterly curse at his own carefreeness for not having prepared a backup plan despite knowing that something like this could happen.
Haaaah, he whined in his heart. I’d already gotten carried away with this whole invincible mode I thought I was in last time… Man, I don’t ever learn, huh?
Was pushing his brain so far into a corner to avoid reality a form of self-defense? Because mocking himself like this felt strangely out of place even to Masachika.

Still continuing to mock himself, Masachika stepped onto the stage. However, the moment he laid eyes on the rows of students beyond the dazzling lights… a single secret plan suddenly hatched in his otherwise empty head.
The sort of plan that made him derisively chuckle on the inside.
No way… I’m actually gonna have to do something like that.
Alea iacta est. Masachika slowly drew in a breath before unleashing his voice toward the microphone…
This… is pretty bad, is it not? Sayaka discretely furrowed her brow as she joined the surrounding students in applauding Yuki and Ayano.

Having promised to cooperate with the new student council should Alisa win the election, Sayaka had already heard her campaign promise in advance. It was something that she certainly felt would leave a huge impact on the student body, but… only in the case of the audience being prepared to listen.
And here I was thinking this would be a close contest up until those two gave their speeches…

Because the reality was that the atmosphere had not been bad at all right up until then. The number of people who viewed Alisa in a positive light had increased noticeably thanks to her accomplishments during the cultural festival and how she had carried herself in the recent student assembly, after all; you could even hear many voices anticipating what kind of speech she would be giving today.
But now…

Those presently gathered were now deeply moved by Yuki and Ayano, their hearts completely swept away in the tide of their speeches. At this point, Alisa’s words would most likely fail to even register in the minds of the audience when they were so caught up in this sort of excitement.
Neither Nono-chan nor I will be lending a hand this time, okay…? Sayaka murmured to herself. Are you really going to be fine?

It was only after she begged that question in her heart did Sayaka realize something: somewhere along the way, she had begun to think from the perspective of someone rooting for Alisa and Masachika as if it were second nature.
Wh-what am I even doing…? Did being in a band together make me soften up to her or something…?
Overcome by what could only be described by panic, Sayaka gave her head a small shake before turning her gaze back toward the stage.
I mean, it’s not like I’m cheering for them or anything… I merely just don’t want to see my friends make a fool of themselves, that’s all…

As she found herself mouthing off excuses to no one in particular, the emcee finally called on Alisa’s name, thinning the buzzing excitement rippling through the gymnasium into only a few scattered whispers.
However…
For some reason, it was Masachika who stepped onto the stage.
“Hm?” Sayaka murmured, involuntarily letting her confusion slip, the students around her seeming equally bewildered.
“Eh?”
“Huh?”
“Why Kuze?”
Yet, amidst all that chatter, she immediately grasped Masachika’s intentions.
Ah, I understand. He’s realized that even Alisa-san speaking in this atmosphere wouldn’t have much of an effect.
In other words, he would step out first to change the mood before handing things over to her.
Easier said than done…

It was simply just as hard for Masachika to get people to listen amidst the current mood as well, after all. Sure, his unexpected appearance had certainly piqued their interests, but it still wasn’t enough to cool the excitement that clouded their heads.
Just how on earth is he planning to turn things around from here…? Sayaka asked herself.
As she watched on with half interest and half concern, Masachika finally opened his mouth atop the stage.

【Дорогие друзья，позвольте представиться．Меня зовут Кудзэ Масатика．Я из общего отдела ученического совета． Разрешите поприветствовать вас в качестве доверенного лица кандидата в председатели совета Кудзё Алисы．】
Soooo much Russian. The students collectively blanked. Sayaka, too, stood frozen with her mouth slightly agape.
“Sorry,” Masachika paused for a moment with a soft chuckle. “I was so nervous I actually started speaking in Russian.”
Laughter erupted throughout the entire gymnasium.
“No way that just happens!” a voice that sounded extremely familiar came flying out somewhere in the crowd.
Even Sayaka couldn’t help but let out a laugh.

Feeling the atmosphere relax all at once, Masachika raised both hands with an easy going smile. “Now then, once again, I’m Masachika Kuze, the student council’s officer for general affairs. Oh, that Russian just now? I did have some help from this translation website, okay? Trying to memorize it by ear’s actually super difficult though, y’knooow? Pronouncing words in Russian is seeeriously rough.”
Sticking his tongue out briefly and shrugging in shoulders in an exaggerated, comical manner, Masachika drew another round of laughter.

“Now then, everyone,” he continued in a casual tone. “You’re all surely wondering why I stepped out here first, aren’t you? Ah, and just to be clear, our emcee here didn’t get the order wrong: this was entirely our own doing. Don’t go havin’ that misunderstanding, ’kay?”
Pressing his palms together toward the emcee, he lowered his head into a bow. “Sorry for taking liberties like thiiiis.”
Clearing his throat lightly, he faced back toward the audience.

“Now then, to start over, as for why I stepped out here first… Well, there’s only one reason.” The casual air vanished from his voice. “Before my partner here speaks about her campaign promise, I wanted you all to prepare yourselves for what you’re about to hear.”

Having heard a little about the plan beforehand, Sayaka knew that Masachika’s appearance before Alisa had been completely unplanned. Yet, Masachika gave no sign of that whatsoever. His tone and demeanor told the tale that everything was proceeding exactly according to schedule, speaking slowly and carefully as if teaching the audience step by step.

“The campaign promise that Alisa Kujou will be about to present is exceptionally ambitious and—among all past student council presidential candidates—incredibly unconventional and different. I think you all will struggle to understand it at first too. Like, ‘Can you even do something like that?’ Some of you might naturally beg the question. I sure did. Honestly, I couldn’t fully wrap my own head around it initially when I first heard what she was aiming for from her own lips.”

Confusion spread among the students at what was an utterly bizarre speech for a student council member’s address. Yet, through that confusion, Sayaka could sense the fervor that had dominated the gymnasium moments earlier being completely rinsed away.

“But,” Masachika continued in clear signal that he was not done, “after listening to her explain all the details and coming to understand what she’s aiming for, for what kind of student council she’s seeking to create… it became something that felt truly wonderful to me as well. I became convinced that it was something worth pursuing seriously—right from the bottom of my heart—and firmly resolved myself to help achieve it.”
Sweeping his gaze across the crowd as confused glances darted from face to face, Masachika anchored the restless room with a low, deliberate cadence.

“I want to tell you all this beforehand: we are absolutely serious. We are entering this presidential election earnestly with this promise, and we fully intend to make it a reality. So please, without laughing it off as empty grandstanding, please listen to her words with an open mind. That’s all from me. Thank you all very much for listening.”
Tch, I’m pathetic, huh…?
Facing the sparse round of applause ringing out here and there, Masachika trotted back toward the wings of the stage, his heart overcome with bitterness.

In the end, all he had managed to do was reset the atmosphere and bring things back to square one. And that was at best. From here, everything else had to be entrusted entirely to his partner. To him, all he could see in the moment were things he should reflect on.
“Good work,” came Alisa’s voice.
“Yeah…” Masachika murmured, returning with his head lowered in apology. “Sorry; I wasn’t much help.”
“That’s not true,” his partner simply shook her head and smiled. “To improvise like that and go that far… I don’t think I could’ve done it myself; you really helped me out.”

Though her words eased him a little, the reality remained that he had been forced to improvise in the first place because he had been caught flat-footed. His bitter expression refused to soften, unable to shake the immense sense of responsibility that weighed on him. Seeing him like that, Alisa offered a faint smile.

“Geez, don’t make that face,” she nudged his shoulder gently. “I never expected Yuki-san and Ayano-san’s speeches to be that impressive either. It isn’t your responsibility alone; we’re a pair, after all… As long as the two of us can combine our strengths to achieve the best possible result, it’ll be okay. I’m right, aren’t I?”
Her gentle question allowed Masachika to finally manage a small smile. “Yeah…” he nodded. “You’re right.”
“Yes. Now’s your turn to watch me, okay?”
No sooner had Alisa said that than the emcee’s announcement rang out.
“Once again, the student council’s treasurer, Alisa Kujou-san, will now give her address.”
Seeing Alisa turn toward the stage, Masachika caught her eye and gave her a small nod.
“Good luck,” he said, his brief words carrying all the faith he had in her.
“Yes,” Alisa let out a soft breath. “Well then…”
Cutting her own words off at that point… she turned back with a small smile.
“I’ll go win this real quick.”
As Alisa stepped onto the stage, countless gazes filled with a mix of curiosity and anticipating turned toward her.
How would she clear the impossibly high bar that Masachika’s introduction had raised?
What exactly was this campaign promise he had spoken of?
Everyone eagerly waited for the moment that answer would finally be revealed.

“As I had been introduced, I am Alisa Kujou, the student council’s treasurer. Today, I would like to take this opportunity to broach the policies I intend to implement should I be elected student council president for the coming year.”

Her words pushed the audience’s anticipation to a fever pitch. The atmosphere was immense and trampled over her from all sides. Nevertheless, Alisa continued calmly, not dropping her unwavering conviction.
“I will,” she paused, gripping the edges of the podium, “abolish the system that limits eligibility for admission into the Raikoukai to only the student council president and vice president.”
Silence. That was all that swept across the students. Even after Masachika’s lengthy preface, most were unable to fully process the bold declaration she had just made, remaining sat frozen in place.

“Beyond just the president and vice president…” Alisa leaned forward, her voice cutting through the gymnasium with absolute certainty, “any student within the student council who has achieved accomplishments worthy of earning such a qualification will be allowed to join the Raikoukai.”
It was only with this nail in the coffin that most of the students began to understand what Alisa was putting on the table…
Yet, at the same time, another wave of confusion erupted among them.
“H-huh?”
“Wha? What did she just say?”
“Uh? Wh-what does she mean?”
Their bewilderment was only natural.

Because simply put, at first glance, Alisa’s promise offered no apparent benefit to herself at all. Even if she became student council president and secured her own ticket to being part of the Raikoukai, what was possibly in it for her in petitioning them to extend that same ticket to others? If anything, one would think it offered nothing but risk: the possibility of having her own qualification revoked.
For students at this school, the reason for aspiring to become the student council president was, first and foremost, entry into the Raikoukai. That was the fundamental premise.

Some wanted to join to secure a stable future. Others wanted to join as it was key to making their dreams come true. A number sought admission because it was a duty imposed upon them by their parents.
The details varied from person to person, but the bottom line was that everyone shared the same goal: they wanted to join the Raikoukai.

As a result, those who were elected student council president basically never did anything that could be seen as challenging the Raikoukai themselves. Much less would an ordinary student dare interfere with the very structure of the organization itself.
“Could it be… she wants someone other than herself and Kuze to join the Raikoukai too?” one student suggested.
“Oh…” another wondered. “Is that what this is?”
Though still confused, the audience desperately searched for an explanation that made sense. After hearing the murmurs settle down somewhat, Alisa began with her rationale.
“Since enrolling in this school and working within the student council as one of the candidates for president… I have come to meet many who aspire to join the Raikoukai.”
Pausing briefly, Alisa faced the collective gaze of the audience head on.

“People who have ruthlessly trampled over others in a bid to join the Raikoukai,” she spoke each word as though savoring their weight. “People who have dragged the entire academy into turmoil in the pursuit of admission. People who have lost their qualification to join and, after much anguish, went down the wrong path.”
Sayaka Taniyama, whom she had once faced in a debate and now counted as a friend.
Yuusho Kiryuuin, once an enemy whom she later temporarily joined forces with.
Taiki Kaji, whose circumstances Yuki had once spoken of with a tinge of blue in her voice.
“And people,” Alisa spoke on, “who despite deeply caring for each other… ended up in conflict over who would join the Raikoukai.”

They were, of course… Masachika and Yuki: a brother and sister who loved one another, yet found themselves clashing over who would join the Raikoukai and inherit the Suou family. And Ayano too, caught in between them, equally devoted to both siblings.
And then there was Masachika himself, who still suffered as he wrestled with his own feelings.
Recalling all their faces, Alisa could only harden her eyes as she spoke, driven by a sense of duty that tugged at her heart.

“I… want to create a system in which all of them can join hands and work together. I want to give these candidates—those who had no choice but to compete against and fight each other—the choice to cooperate.”
So that close friends would not have to become rivals. So that, instead of dragging each other down, they could shoot for the Raikoukai together.

“If we can do that, this school will surely become an even better place! Even if there are limits to what a president and vice president can accomplish, to what two people can do alone, imagine having two pairs, three pairs, all possessing the same level of strength: surely we can achieve so much more! This,” Alisa paused, the word hanging in the air as her resolve shone through, “is the type of student council that I want to build!”
Hearing her plea, one that almost sounded like a cry from the heart, the audience finally came to understand the type of student council that Alisa idealized.

tr: İlk dönemin kapanış töreninde Sayaka ve Nonoa ile omuz omuza durduğu sahne. ve Masachika’nın o sırada Yuki ve Ayano’yu kendi çevrelerine getirmeyi öneren sözleri, Alisa’nın şu anda bahsettiği şeyin kanıtıydı: İkisinin o zamanlar bu okulda norm olarak hayal ettiği yeni bir öğrenci konseyi oluşturmak.
Kesinlikle çok büyük bir hırstı… Rüya gibi bir fantezi.
“İlk dönemin kapanış töreninde şunu söylemiştim: Öğrenci konseyi başkanlığına layık olmadığıma inanamıyorsam, kendi isteğimle seçimden çekileceğim.”
Bu, Alisa’nın bir zamanlar beyan ettiği bir karardı, ancak şimdi bunun üzerine daha da büyük bir karar koymaya çalışıyordu.

Bir elini göğsüne koyarak, “Bu sözleri geri alıyorum,” diye duyurdu. “Değerli olup olmamamın bir önemi yok. Öğrenci konseyi başkanı olmam gerekiyor çünkü hayal ettiğim öğrenci konseyi - hayal ettiğim Seirei Akademisi - şu andan çok daha zarif, daha eğlenceli olacak! Ve bu ideali gerçeğe dönüştürebilecek tek kişi benim!”
Bu sadece benim yapabileceğim bir şey, çünkü bu yarışta Raikoukai’ye katılmak için değil, sadece öğrenci konseyi başkanı olmak için öğrenci konseyi başkanı olmak için koşan tek kişi benim!“”

Sözleri o kadar büyük bir güçle ifade edilmişti ki galiba dinleyicilere değil de kendisine yöneltilmiş haldeydi. Bu onun karakterinin bir kanıtıydı: dinleyenlerin onayı veya sempatisi olmadan ideallerinin peşinde koşan biri.

Alisa yoğun bir gururla yukarıya bakarken, “Bulduğum bu ideale sadık kalacağım,” diye ilan etti. “Bunu gerçeğe dönüştürmek için elimden gelen tüm çabayı göstereceğim. Benim gibi birinin öğrenci konseyi başkanı olmaya layık olup olmadığına gelince… Bu kararı hepinize bırakıyorum. Dinlediğiniz için çok teşekkür ederim.”

Alisa başını eğerek sahneden indi ama o uzaklaşmaya başladığında tüm öğrenciler oldukları yerde donup kaldılar. Konuşma yeteneklerini tamamen kaybetmişlerdi, böylesi bir gösteri karşısında son derece şaşkına dönmüşlerdi ve onun gidişini yalnızca sessizce izleyebiliyorlardı.

Ancak Masachika kanatlardan çıkıp selam vererek yanında durduktan sonra nihayet kalabalığın içinden bir yerden birkaç alkış yükseldi ve yavaş yavaş spor salonundan üzerlerine yavaşça yağan bir alkışa dönüştü.
Elbette, Yuki ve Ayano’nun aldığı alkışlarda duyulan sesin aynısını içermiyordu ama orada bulunan hiç kimse bunu umursamadı.
Çünkü herkes alkışlıyordu.
Aradaki fark yalnızca alkışların niteliğindeydi.
Yuki ve Ayano’ya dair alkışlar bir coşku duygusu taşıyordu.
Alisa ve Masachika’ya yöneltilen alkışlar saygı amaçlıydı.
Muazzam bir idealin ağırlığını taşıyarak ilerleyen iki insana saygı dolu bir alkış: Onları kollayanlardan… Seyretmek dışında hiçbir şey yapamayanlardan.
Sonuçta her iki taraf da kapanış töreninden diğerine açık bir üstünlükle çıkamadı… Ancak buna rağmen herkes tek bir kanaati paylaşarak ayrıldı.
Alisa Kujou veya Yuki Suou’nun bir sonraki öğrenci konseyi başkanı olacağına dair inanç. Ve sonuçta bu ikisinden hangisi böyle bir pozisyonu iddia ederse etsin, Seirei Akademisi şüphesiz değişecekti.
Öğrencilerin heyecanı giderek güçlenirken ikinci yarıyılın kapanış töreni sona erdi.
en: The scene of her standing shoulder to shoulder with Sayaka and Nonoa during the first semester’s closing ceremony. and the words that Masachika had offered, suggesting to bring Yuki and Ayano into their circle at the time, were evidence to what Alisa was speaking about now: making a new student council, one that the two of them had envisioned back then, the norm at this school.
It was certainly an ambition that was vast… A dreamlike fantasy.
“I had said this during the first semester’s closing ceremony: if I could not believe myself as worthy of being student council president, then I will withdraw from the election by my own accord.”
It was a resolve that Alisa had once declared, yet one she now sought to overwrite with one even greater.

“I retract these words,” she announced, placing one hand over her chest. “Whether I’m worthy or not is irrelevant. I have to become the student council president, for the student council that I envision—the Seirei Academy that I envision—will surely be more graceful, more enjoyable, than it is now! And because I am the only one who can make that ideal a reality! It is something that only I can do, for I am the only person with a foot in this race running not to join the Raikoukai, but to simply become student council president for the sake of being the student council president!”

Her words were delivered with such an immense force that they seemed to be directed not at the audience, but at herself. It bore testament to her character: someone who sought for her ideals without the approval or sympathy of those who listened.

“I will remain true to this ideal that I have found,” Alisa proclaimed, gazing upward with an intense pride. “I will devote nothing but my utmost effort into making it a reality. As for whether someone like me is worthy of becoming the student council president… I’ll leave that judgement to all of you. Thank you very much for listening.”

Bowing her head, Alisa stepped down from the stage, and yet, even as she began to walk away, all the students remained frozen in place. They had completely lost their abilities to speak, utterly overwhelmed by such a display and could only watch her departure in silence.

It was only after Masachika emerged from the wings to stand beside her in a bow did a few claps finally rise from somewhere within the crowd, gradually growing across the gymnasium into an applause that gently rained down upon them.
Sure, it did not harbor the same sheer volume heard in the ovation that Yuki and Ayano had received, but nobody present cared about that.
Because everyone was applauding.
The difference was merely in the nature of the applause.
The ovation directed at Yuki and Ayano had carried a sense of enthusiasm.
The applause now directed at Alisa and Masachika was one of respect.
An applause full of respect for two people walking forward while carrying the weight of an immense ideal: an applause from those who watched over them… From those who could do nothing but watch.
In the end, neither pair emerged from the closing ceremony with a clear advantage over the other… But even so, in spite of this, everyone came away sharing a single conviction.

A conviction that either Alisa Kujou or Yuki Suou would become the next student council president. And that no matter which of the two would ultimately claim such a position, Seirei Academy would undoubtedly change.
With the students’ anticipation quietly growing stronger… the second semester’s closing ceremony came to a close.

tr: “Evet… Bu pek doğru gelmiyor, ha…?”

Şu anda kapanış töreninden sonraydı. Yuki’nin Noel partisi için mekanın hazırlanmasına yardım etmeyi bitiren Masachika, kendini yalnız buldu. Erkekler tuvaletindeki bir aynanın önünde durdu, dudakları ince bir çizgiye bastırılmıştı.

Baharda resmi davetler için aldığı bir takım elbise giyiyordu. Sıradan insanların tam olarak ucuz diyeceği bir şey değildi ama özel yapım olmak yerine hâlâ kullanıma hazır olması, büyük ihtimalle bu okulun standartlarına göre onu bu şekilde nitelendiriyordu.

En azından saçlarını düzgünce bir araya getirmeye çalışan Masachika, inatçı saç tellerine beceriksizce saç balmumu uyguladı; bu, kullanmaya hiç alışmadığı bir şeydi. Ancak… ne kadar çabalarsa çabalasın, istediği gibi kalmayacaktı.
“Ama evde denediğimde biraz daha iyi oldu…” diye mırıldandı.
Yüzünü buruşturup farklı yaptığı şey için beynini zorladı, ancak banyo yaptıktan hemen sonra pratik yaptığını fark etti.
Ha? Durun, hayır… saçınızın ne kadar temiz olması aslında bu kadar fark yaratır mı?
Hoş olmayan düşünce yavaşça sırtının soğuk terlerle dolmasına neden oldu.
Hayır, ama çocukken piyano resitalleri ve benzeri şeyler için gayet iyi yapardım…
Uzun zaman öncesine ait bulanık anılara güvenen Masachika, saçıyla oynamaya devam etti.
Ha? O zamanlar bunu nasıl yapmıştım? Ben…böyle yaptığımdan oldukça eminim…
Ancak, düşündüğünüz gibi, yine de işe yaramayacak. Belki de tüm balmumunu yıkayıp baştan başlamak burada akıllıca bir seçimdi.
Ama yine de saçını yıkamak istese bile bunu okulda yapmak biraz… anlıyor musun? Üstelik ilk etapta fazla zaman kalmamıştı.
Durun, olmaz… Bu çok güzel değil mi… hayır, cidden kötü mü?
Panik onu ele geçirdiğinde omurgasından aşağı bir ürperti yayıldı, kalbi aşırı hızlanmaya başladı.
Aaargh, kahretsin. Önce kapanış töreni ve şimdi de bu… Hazırlık eksikliğim çok fazla! Cidden, ben ne yapıyorum!?

Alisa’nın kampanya vaadini duyduğundan beri Masachika, içine düştüğü bu sözde “yenilmez mod”un satın aldığı sonsuz motivasyonla bugüne kadar güç kazanmıştı. Onun sayesinde düne kadar her şeyin yolunda gittiğini hissediyordu; ister dersleri, ister öğrenci konseyi çalışmaları, hatta rüzgar topluluğu kulübüyle antrenmanlar olsun.

Ancak şimdi, asıl önemli olan güne gelindiğinde, onu hareket ettiren -ileriye doğru attığı her adımı tökezleyemeyeceğinin yadsınamaz bir kanıtı gibi hissettiren- o tünel görüşü nihayet muhteşem biçimde geri gelip onu ısırmaya başlamıştı.
Aaargh, Tanrım!

İşlerin yolunda gitmeyeceğini haykırarak saçından bir tutamı sıkan Masachika, acı kendisine karşı hissettiği hayal kırıklığının yanında odaklanabileceği başka bir şey verene kadar tutuşunu daha da sıkılaştırdı.
“Gerçekten ne yapıyorsun sen Kuze?” Kafasındaki gürültünün arasından bir ses kendine yol açtı.
Yuusho’dan başkasına ait değildi. Bir noktada, kollarını kavuşturmuş halde tuvaletin duvarına yaslanarak içeri girmişti.
“…Neden buradasın dostum?” Masachika aynadaki yansımasını gördü; gözleri bir haftalık bir fincan kahve kadar düzdü.
“Neden dedin? Ben sadece Sumire-neesan’a eşlik ediyordum; sadece kendi işimi yapmak için buradayım, tamam mı?”
“Evet, elbette.”
“Bu bir yana…” Yuusho omuz silkti, ağzında bir sırıtış vardı: “Siz ikiniz kesinlikle büyük kampanya sözünü yerine getirdiniz, hm?”
Sesindeki alaycı ifade, gözlerindeki alaycılıkla eşleşiyordu.
“İkiniz de ciddi olarak bunu gerçekleştirebileceğinize inanıyor musunuz?”
Masachika gözünü bile kırpmadı. “Bunu yapıp yapamayacağımız değil. Yapacağız.”
“…Hımmm?”
Kesin beyanı o kadar belirsiz bir uğultuyla karşılandı ki Yuusho’nun bunu satın alıp almadığını söylemek imkansız hale geldi.

“Ah pekala, bu başlı başına başka bir mesele…” Yuusho elini yavaşça salladı ve gözlerini Masachika’nın başına doğru kaydırırken gözlerini kıstı. “Senin saçın ne? Bir beyefendinin mutlaka kendi saçını yapabilmesi gerekir, öyle değil mi? Ama yine de…”
Masachika’nın saç felaketini bir kez daha incelemek için durduğunda dramatik biçimde kaşını kaldırdı.
Bu o kadar gösterişli bir jestti ki Masachika normalde bir an bile tereddüt etmeden karşılık verirdi. Ancak bu sefer tartışmaya yer olmadığından sessizliğin kendisi adına cevap vermesine izin verdi.
Onun çabuk ve teslimiyetle teslim olduğunu gören Yuusho abartılı biçimde başını salladı ve bıkkın bir iç çekişle kendini duvardan itti.
“Ah canım, ah canım. Rakibim olması gereken bir adamın böyle saçlı bir partiye gelmesine pek izin veremem, değil mi?”
Ne zamandan beri senin rakibin oldum? Bu soru Masachika’nın aklına geldi. Ve tuhaf saçlı olan da sensin.
Yine de Yuusho’nun ne yapmak üzere olduğunu fark ederek iğnelerini yuttu ve onların dişlerinin ardında ölmelerine izin verdi.
“İşte, kafanı biraz eğ.”

Mascahika kendisine söyleneni yaparak dizlerini hafifçe büktü ve Yuusho’nun parmaklarıyla az miktarda saç balmumunu kürekle atmasına ve ardından parmaklarını saçlarının arasından geçirmesine izin vererek aynadaki yansımayı yakından gözlemledi. Ağdayı güvenle uyguladı, saçlarına hacim kazandırdı ve olağanüstü bir kolaylıkla şekillendirdi.
“Hımm… Ah, ideal olarak saçını kurutmakla başlamalıydık ama… sanırım şimdilik bu işe yarar, ha?”

Her ne kadar hâlâ o kadar tatmin olmuş gibi görünmese de Yuusho sonunda ellerini ceplerine götürdü. Kendi standartlarına zar zor ulaşabiliyordu ama Masahika’nın evde hayal edebildiğinden çok daha iyi duruyordu.
“…Teşekkürler dostum. Bunu bu sefer dürüstçe söyleyeceğim Kiryuuin.”
“Öyle mi? Öyleyse bir dahaki sefere bunu kendi başına yapabileceğinden emin ol, tamam mı?”
“…Evet. Cidden, teşekkür ederim.”
Yuusho’ya bir kez daha teşekkür edip ellerini yıkayan Masachika, aceleyle Sınıf 1-B’ye doğru ilerledi.
“Vay be… Tanrıya şükür. Henüz burada değil.”
Sınıfın kapısını kaydırarak açtı ve rahat bir nefes aldı; beklediği ortağın henüz gelmediğini fark ettikten sonra omuzları nihayet gevşedi. Saate baktı. 15:40

Parti 4:30’da başlıyor, kapılar da… dur, saat 3:30’du, değil mi? Muhtemelen yakında oraya giderim… Hayır, durun, Alya ve ben etkinlik ekibinin bir parçası bile değiliz; oraya erken gitmemize gerek yok…
Aklında bu düşünceyle Masachika okul bahçesine baktı, hâlâ tam olarak yerleşememişti. Zarif giyimli öğrenciler, uzaktan ön kapının ötesine birbiri ardına geldiler.
Oooh… Tam da zengin çocuklarla dolu bir okuldan bekleyeceğiniz şey. Herkes gerçekten buraya gidiyor, ha…?

Sıradan takım elbisesine bakan Masachika bir kez daha başka bir dünyaya gitmiş gibi hissetti. Yine de dökülen süt için ağlamanın bir anlamı yoktu. En azından kendini güvenle taşıması gerekiyordu. Ve tıpkı Suou ailesinde geçirdiği günlerden itibaren kendisine aşılanan görgü kurallarını ve davranışları hatırladığında…
Vızıltı.
Titreşim bacağına çarptı.
“Hım?”
Yaklaşık iki atıştan sonra durdu. Cebinden telefonunu çıkaran Masachika, Alisa’dan gelen tek bir mesajı gördü.
Gel beni al.
“Gelip seni alayım… Ne, öğrenci konseyi ofisinden mi?”

Alisa da dahil olmak üzere öğrenci konseyindeki tüm kızlar, öğrenci konseyi odasındaki partiye hazırlanıyorlardı. Bu doğal olarak ve açıkça değişimi de içeriyordu. Bu, Masachika’nın olduğu yerde donup kalmasına ve sırf ondan istediği için oraya gitmenin gerçekten sorun olup olmadığı hakkında bir an tereddüt etmesine neden oldu.

“Yani… eğer bana gelmemi söylüyorsa şimdiye kadar herkesin işi bitmiştir, değil mi?” diye mırıldandı, sözleri daha çok kendi kendine yaptığı bir tartışmaya benziyordu. “Ama mesela neden onu almama ihtiyacı var…?”
Kafasını şaşkınlıkla sallayarak sınıftan çıktı ve öğrenci konseyi ofisine doğru ilerledi.
Çok geçmeden kapıyı çaldı.
“Evet” diye cevap verdi içeriden bir ses. Kapıyı ardına kadar açtı.
“Alya? Bir şey mi oldu… kalem…?”
İçeride duran kıza baktığı anda bu soru silinip gitti.
“Ah,” Alisa ona gülümseyerek baktı. “Teşekkür ederim Masachika-kun.”

Gece elbisesi giymişti ve saçları örgülü bir topuz şeklinde toplanmıştı. Yaptığı hafif makyajın da yardımıyla her zamankinden daha olgun duruyordu. Her şeyden önemlisi… o kadar şaşırtıcı derecede güzeldi ki, bu onun sözlerini elinden aldı.
Ha…? O… biraz… farklı mı hissediyor, bir yolunu bulup?

Masachika’yı etkileyen izlenim, onu kültür festivalinin parti sonrası partisinde elbiseyle gördüğü zamanki izleniminden tamamen farklıydı. Ve bu kesinlikle saç modeli ya da makyajından dolayı değildi…
Bunun yerine Alisa’nın içinden parlayan ışıltıdaki farklılıktı.
Özellikle bu… bir tür kırılgan… ya da daha doğrusu onun savunmasız tarafı…? Gitmiş gibi…

Genellikle çevresinde çiçek açıyormuş gibi görünen ruhani, neredeyse göksel aurası tamamen dağılmış, yerini güven ve gururdan yeşeren ağırbaşlı bir zarafet almıştı. Sanki bir peri yeryüzüne inip insana dönüşmüştü… İşte bu yüzden güzelliği gerçeklikten daha da kopmuştu.
“Masachika-kun mu?” Masahika’nın sersemlettiği peri, onun düştüğü büyüyü bozdu.
“Ah, hayır, uh…” sözleri üzerine tökezledi. “Ah, ımm… sadece, gerçekten çok güzel görünüyorsun.”
“O-oh? Teşekkür ederim… Um, Masachika-kun, sen de harika görünüyorsun, biliyor musun?”

Alisa belki de onun alışılmadık şekilde telaşlı tavrının gerçekten yürekten konuştuğu anlamına geldiğini fark ederek utangaçça bakışlarını kaçırdı. Onun ani utangaçlığı dudaklarında hafif bir gülümsemeye neden oldu ve midesinde uçuşan kelebekleri hafifletti.
“Haaah…” rahat bir nefes aldı. “Teşekkürler.”
Boğazını temizlemek için bir süre bekledikten sonra daha önce sorduğu soruyu tekrarladı.
“Uhhh, bir şey mi oldu? Gelip seni almamı söylemiştin…”
“Ha? Ah, bu konuda…”
Saçını parmağının etrafında döndüren Alisa utangaçça bakışlarını bir kez daha kaçırdı.
[Ben sadece… beni ilk gören sen olmanı istedim…] diye mırıldandı.
Ah!

Bu dünyanın ötesinde görünen çok güzel bir kızın dudaklarından dökülen Rusça söylenen bu dayanılmaz derecede sevecen sözler, Masachika’yı neredeyse boğuyordu. Yine de bir yolunu bulup soğukkanlılığını korumayı başardı ve her zamanki tepkisini verdi.
“Neydi o?”
“Bir bayanı alıp ona eşlik etmenin bir beyefendinin görevi olduğunu söylemiştim, değil mi?”
“Ah, doğru, değil mi?”

Alisa’nın dudaklarından “beyefendi” kelimesinin çıktığını duyan Masachika, Suou ailesinin çocukluğunda ona zarifçe kolunu uzatırken ona aşıladığı görgü kurallarının her birinden yararlanarak sessizce kendini toparladı.
“Gidelim mi?”
“E-evet.”
Belki onun yumuşak, beklenmedik şekilde gösterişli hareketlerinden biraz korkan Alisa çekingence kolunu uzattı…
Sadece bazı nedenlerden dolayı onu geri çekmek için.
“Hm? Alya?” Masachika ona şaşkın bir bakış attı.
Hiçbir tepki vermedi ve gözlerini indirdi, düşünceleri çok uzak bir yere sürükleniyormuş gibi bakışlarından kaçtı.
“Bugün… Noel Arifesi, değil mi…?”
Sözleri tereddütlüydü ve sesi titriyordu, her hece boğazında düğümleniyordu.
Masachika yalnızca bir kez göz kırpabildi. “Evet.”
Başını yana eğdi ve kız onun önünde durup sessizliğini korurken neden bu kadar bariz bir şeyi gündeme getirdiğini anlamak için yüzüne baktı.
Bir saniye önce ikiye, sonra birkaç saniyeye dönüştü.
Sonra birdenbire başını kaldırdı ve tuhaf biçimde sarsılmaz bir bakışla ona sıkı sıkıya sarıldı.
“Biraz dışarı çık!”
“Ha? Ne…?”
“Sadece yap!”
Hiçbir uyarıda bulunmadan onu odadan dışarı itti ve kapıyı çarparak kapattı ve Masachika’yı ağzı açık halde orada bıraktı.
“U-uhhh…?”
“Orada bekle! Ne olursa olsun, ben çağırana kadar kapıyı açmayın! Kim gelirse gelsin!”
“Ah… tamam.”
Bir yolunu bulup onu yanlış şekilde mi ovuşturmuştu? Bu fikir bir anlığına aklından geçti ama hemen vazgeçti. Durum böyle görünmüyordu.
Yine de, neler olup bittiğine dair en ufak bir fikri olmamasına rağmen, buradaki bayan ona kapıcı rolünü vermişti, o da onun emirlerine itaatkar biçimde uydu.
On dakikadan biraz fazla bir süre sonra…
“E-artık içeri girebilirsin.”
“Tamam…”
“Ah! Başka kimse yok, değil mi!?”
“Yok ama…”
“A-pekala… İçeri gelin.”
Kapının diğer tarafından sözlerinin altındaki sert gerilimi duyan Masachika, ihtiyatlı biçimde kapı koluna uzandı.
“N-neyin var senin…?”
Yavaşça kapıyı açtı. Alisa diğer tarafta duruyordu.
Ona sadece bakmak bile sözlerini bir kez daha elinden aldı, onu ikinci kez bu şekilde görmesine rağmen güzelliğinin etkisi en ufak bir azalma bile göstermedi…
Ancak şimdi giydiği elbise tamamen değişmişti.

Artık gece gökyüzü kadar mürekkep rengindeydi; karanlık yüzeyi, ufukta çıtırdayan havai fişekler gibi açan mavi gül buketleriyle bölünmüştü. Obsidiyen kumaş, kış gökyüzünün altında yeni yağmış kar gibi cesurca ortaya çıkan, ışıkta parıldayan tertemiz beyaz teniyle tezat oluşturuyordu…
Daha doğrusu göğüsleri! Daha da önemlisi bunlar onun göğüsleriydi!
Çok büyükler! Ah, sutyeni nereye gitti!?

Masachika bu düşünceleri zar zor boğazına doğru iterek aceleyle arkasına uzandı ve kapıyı çarparak kapattı. Ancak bunu yaparken bile gözlerini bildiğin şeyden ayıramıyordu: dışarı doğru cesurca yükselen o muhteşem zirvelerden ve aralarında oluşan çekici vadiden.

Hayır, hayır, sakin ol Masachika. Burada objektif davranırsak Alya, Masha-san’a kıyasla o kadar da iri göğüslü değil. Sadece omuzları ve belinin inanılmaz derecede ince olması onu gerçekte olduğundan daha büyük gösteriyor. Sakin olun, baktığınızda o kadar da büyük değiller…
Hâlâ orada donup kalmış halde duran Masachika, gözlerinin etrafta dolaşmasına izin vermeye devam etti.
Kimi kandırıyorum, çok büyükler. Resmen bir mangadan fırlamış gibi, değil mi?
Durumu olabildiğince mantıklı biçimde analiz etmeye çalıştıktan sonra bile önündeki manzara o kadar akıllara durgunluk vericiydi ki ne yapacağını bilemez haldeydi.
Alisa eteğinin kenarını hafifçe çekiştirirken cilveli bir poz verirken ona alaycı bir tavırla gülümsedi.
Parıldayan beyaz bacağı yavaş yavaş görüş alanına girdi… ve sonra solu da. Süper bir sürpriz.
Hayır, cidden, sutyeni gerçekte nereye gitti!?
Kayışlarının nerede olması gerektiğini bulamayan Masachika’nın kulakları, kaçmasına izin vermediği bir çığlıkla doldu.

Garipti. Elbise, nesnel olarak bir mayonun kaplayabileceğinden çok daha fazlasını kapsıyordu, ancak normal bir mayonun korumaya hizmet edeceği önemli alanlar, yalnızca kağıttan yapılmış bir zırh kadar kırılgan ve çıplaktı. Bu ancak beynini dışarı çıkmanın eşiğine getiren bir dengesizlik olarak tanımlanabilirdi.
Alisa’nın sırıtışı daha da yukarı doğru kıvrıldı.
[Hediyeniz… E… E…♡]

Elbisesi, aysız bir okyanus kadar karanlık olsa da, bir yay gibi keskin bir kavis çizerek beli boyunca uzanırken büyüleyici bir parlaklıkla parlıyordu. Sadece onun yüce güzelliğini çerçevelemek ve vurgulamak için varmış gibi, figürünün yarattığı kıvrımları keskin biçimde vurguluyordu.
Açıkta bıraktığı saf beyaz et parçalarına sadece birkaç göz atmak bile yasadışı ve o kadar… çekici biçimde şehvetli hissettiriyordu ki, Masachika’nın nefesini kesmekle tehdit ediyordu.
Böyle bir görüntü, onun tatlı tatlı Rusça fısıldadığı kur’unun katıksız yıkımıyla birleşince, onu yaz güneşinin altında yakalanmış bir gül gibi kızarmaya fazlasıyla yetti. Zihni dondu.
İkisi ne kadar süre birbirlerine öyle bakmaya devam etti?
Alisa da farkına bile varmadan köprücük kemiğinden göğsüne doğru yavaş yavaş yayılan hafif bir kızarıklıkla parladı…
en: “Yeaaah… This pretty much doesn’t feel right, huh…?”

It was currently after the closing ceremony. Masachika, who had finished helping set up the venue for Yuki’s Christmas party, found himself alone. He stood in front of a mirror in the men’s bathroom, his lips pressed into a thin line.

He wore a suit that he’d bought in the spring for formal occasions. It wasn’t something most ordinary folk would exactly call cheap, but the fact that it was still off-the-rack as opposed to being custom-made most likely qualified it as such by this school’s standards.

Trying to at the very least properly put his hair together, Masachika awkwardly worked hair wax through his stubborn strands, something he never really got used to using. However… no matter how hard he tried, it just wouldn’t stay the way he wanted.
“It had turned out a li’l better when I tried it at home, though…” he muttered.
Scrunching up his face, he racked his brain for what he had done differently, only to realize that he had practiced right after taking a bath.
Huh? Wait, no way… does how clean your hair is actually make that much of a difference?
The unpleasant thought slowly sent his back breaking out in a cold sweat.
No, but, I used to do it just fine for piano recitals and stuff when I was a kid…
Relying on hazy memories from long ago, Masachika continued to fiddle with his hair.
Huh? How did I do it back then again? I’m... pretty sure I did it like this…
Yet, just as you might have thought, it still wouldn’t work out. Perhaps simply washing all the wax out and starting over was the smart choice here.
But still, even if he did want to wash his hair, doing it at school was a little… you know? Besides, there wasn’t much time left in the first place.
Hol’ on, no way… Isn’t this pretty… no, seriously bad?
A chill ran down his spine as panic overtook him, his heart pounding right into overdrive.
Aaargh, shit. First the closing ceremony and now this… My lack of prep’s too much! Seriously, the hell am I doing!?

Ever since hearing Alisa’s campaign promise, Masachika had powered through to this very day on an endless motivation bought on by this so-called “invincible mode” he had fallen into. It was thanks to it that he felt that everything up until yesterday had gone smoothly, whether it was his studies, student council work, or even practice with the wind ensemble club. Yet now, when it came down to the day that actually mattered, the very tunnel vision that had kept him moving—making every step forward feel like undeniable proof that he couldn’t stumble—had finally spectacularly come back to bite him.
Aaargh, geez!!!

Clenching a fistful of his hair in a cry of how things simply would not go his way, Masachika tightened his grip until the pain gave him something else to focus on beside the disappointment he felt toward himself.
“Honestly, what on earth are you doing, Kuze?” a voice forced its way through the noise in his head.
It belonged to none other than Yuusho. He had, at some point, waltzed right in, leaning against the restroom wall with his arms folded.
“…Why the hell are you even here, man?” Masachika caught his reflection in the mirror, his eyes as flat as a week-old cup of coffee.
“Why, you say? I was just escorting Sumire-neesan; I’m simply here to do my own business, okay?”
“Yeah, sure.”
“That aside…” Yuusho shrugged, a smirk tugging at his mouth, “you two sure have made quiiite the grand campaign promise, hm?”
The derisive edge in his voice matched the mockery in his eyes.
“Do you both seriously believe you can make it happen?”
Masachika didn’t so much as blink. “It ain’t about whether we can. We will.”
“…Hmmm?”
His firm declaration was met with a hum so ambiguous that it made it impossible to tell whether Yuusho bought it or not.

“Oh well, that’s another matter in itself…” Yuusho made a languid sweep of his hand, squinting as he moved his eyes up to Masachika’s head. “What’s with that hair of yours? Surely a gentleman ought to be able to style his own hair, don’t you think? And yet…”
Stopping to scrutinize Masachika’s hair disaster once more, he dramatically raised an eyebrow.
It was a gesture so pompous that Masachika would have normally fired back at without a moment of hesitation. But with no room to argue this time, he simply let the silence answer for him.
Seeing his quick and yielding surrender, Yuusho gave an exaggerated shake of his head, pushing himself off the wall with an exasperated sigh.
“Oh dear, oh dear. I can’t very well let a man who’s supposed to be my rival show up to a party with hair like that, can I?”
Since when did I become your rival? The question sprung in Masachika;’s mind. And you’re the one with weird hair.
Still, realizing what Yuusho was about to do, he swallowed his jabs, letting them die behind his teeth.
“Here, lower your head a little.”

Doing as he was told, Mascahika bent his knees slightly, allowing Yuusho to shovel a small amount of hair wax with his fingers before running them through his hair, closely observing the reflection in the mirror. He worked the wax in with confidence, giving volume to his hair and shaping it with remarkable ease.
“Hmm… Oh well, we ideally should’ve started with blowing your hair dry but… I suppose this does it for now, huh?”

Though he still didn’t seem all that satisfied, Yuusho finally took his hands to his pockets. It only barely passed by his own standards, but it looked noticeably better than whatever Masahika had been able to conjure up at home.
“…Thanks man. I’ll say that honestly this time, Kiryuuin.”
“Is that so? Well in that case, make sure you can do it yourself next time, okay?”
“…Yeah. Seriously, thank you.”
Thanking Yuusho once more and washing his hands, Masachika hurried toward Class 1-B.
“Phew… Thank God. She’s not here yet.”

Sliding open the classroom’s door, he let out a sigh of relief, his shoulders finally loosening after observing that the partner that he’d been expecting had yet to arrive. He glanced at the clock. 3:40 p.m.
The party starts at 4:30 while doors open at… wait, it was 3:30, wasn’t it? I should prolly head over soon… No, wait, Alya and I aren’t even part of the event staff; we don’t gotta be there early…
With that thought in mind, Masachika looked out over the school grounds, still unable to quite settle down. Elegantly dressed students arrived one after another beyond the front gate in the distance.
Oooh… Just what you’d expect from a school full of rich kids. Everyone’s reaaaally going all out here, huh…?

Looking down at his off-the-rack suit, Masachika once again felt as if he’d wandered off into another world. Still, there was no point in crying over spilt milk. He had to, at the very least, carry himself with confidence. And just as he recalled the etiquette and bearing drilled into him from his days back in the Suou household…
Buzz.
Vibration rattled against his leg.
“Hm?”
It stopped after about two more pulses. Fishing out his phone from his pocket, Masachika made out a single message from Alisa.
Come pick me up.
“Come pick you up…? What, from the student council office?”

All the girls on the student council—including Alisa—were all preparing for the party in the student council room. That naturally and obviously included changing. It made Masachika stand frozen on the spot, hesitating for a moment over whether it was really okay to go there just because she’d asked him to.

“I mean… surely everyone’s done by now if she’s telling me to come, no?” he murmured, his words sounding more like an argument he was making to himself. “But like, why does she need me to pick her up…?”
Cocking his head in confusion, he left the classroom and made his way over to the student council office.
Arriving in no time, he knocked on the door.
“Yes,” a voice answered from the inside. He swung the door open.
“Alya? Did something hap… pen…?”
The question withered away the instant he laid his eyes on the girl standing inside.
“Ah,” Alisa looked up at him with a smile. “Thank you, Masachika-kun.”

She was dressed in an evening gown, and her hair had been pulled back into a braided updo. She looked even more mature than usual, helped along by the light touch of makeup she wore. More than anything… she was so stunningly beautiful that it robbed him of his words.
Huh…? She… feels a little… different, somehow?
The impression that struck Masachika felt completely different from when he had seen her in a dress at the cultural festival’s after party. And it surely wasn’t because of her hairstyle or makeup…
It was instead the difference in the radiance that shone from within Alisa herself.
Specifically that… sort of fragile… or rather vulnerable side to her…? It’s as if it’s gone…

Her ethereal, almost celestial aura that usually seemed to bloom around her had completely dissipated, a dignified grace that blossomed from confidence and pride unfurling in its place. It was as though a fairy had descended to earth and became human… And it was precisely because of that reason that her beauty felt even all the more detached from reality.
“Masachika-kun?” The very fairy Masahika had been dazing over broke the spell he had fallen under.
“Ah, no, uh…” he stumbled over his words. “Ah, um… it’s just, you look absolutely beautiful.”
“O-oh? Thank you… Um, Masachika-kun, you look great too, you know?”

Perhaps realizing that his unusually flustered demeanor meant that he was truly speaking from the heart, Alisa bashfully averted her gaze. Her sudden shyness brought a faint smile to his lips, easing the butterflies that had been fluttering in his stomach.
“Haaah…” he let a sigh of relief escape. “Thanks.”
Taking a moment to clear his throat, he repeated the question he’d asked earlier.
“Uhhh, did something happen? You said to come pick you up…”
“Eh? Ah, about that…”
Twirling her hair around her finger, Alisa bashfully averted her gaze once more.
【I just… wanted you to be the first to see me…】 she murmured under her breath.
Gah!

Those unbearably endearing words, spoken in Russian as they slipped from the lips of a girl so beautiful she seemed beyond this world nearly made Masachika choke. Even so, he somehow managed to hold his composure by a thread, delivering his customary response.
“What was that?”
“I said it’s a gentleman’s duty to pick up and escort a lady, is it not?”
“Ah, that’s right, isn’t it?”

Hearing the very word “gentleman” spoken from Alisa’s lips, Masachika quietly gathered himself, drawing upon every bit of etiquette the Suou household had drilled into him as a kid as he gracefully offered her his arm.
“Shall we?”
“Y-yes.”
Maybe a little intimidated by his smooth, unexpectedly polished movements, Alisa timidly reached her arm out…
Only to, for some reason, pull it back.
“Hm? Alya?” Masachika cast a puzzled glance her way.
She gave no response and lowered her eyes, dodging his gaze as her thoughts seemed to drift somewhere far away.
“Today is… Christmas Eve, isn’t it…?”
Her words were hesitant and her voice shook, each syllable catching in her throat.
Masachika could only blink once. “Yeah.”
He cocked his head to its side, searching her face as to why she was bringing something so obvious up now, while the very girl stood before him and held her silence.
One second turned to two, and then to several.
Then, all at once, she raised her head, holding him firmly in an oddly unwavering gaze.
“Step outside for a bit!”
“Huh? Wha—?”
“Just do it!”
Without warning, she shoved him out of the room and slammed the door shut, leaving Masachika standing there with his mouth hanging open.
“U-uhhh…?”
“Wait there! Whatever happens, don’t open the door until I call you! No matter who comes!
“Uh… okay.”
Had he somehow rubbed her the wrong way? The thought crossed his mind for a moment, but he quickly dismissed it. It didn’t seem to be the case.
Still, despite not having the foggiest idea what was going on, the lady here had assigned him the role of doorman, so he obediently followed her orders.
A little over ten minutes later…
“Y-you’re okay to come in now.”
“Oka—”
“Ah! There’s no one else, right!?”
“There isn’t, but…”
“A-alright… Come in.”
Hearing the stiff tension beneath her words from the other side of the door, Masachika cautiously reached for the handle.
“W-what’s up with you…?”
Slowly, he opened the door. Alisa stood on the other side.
Merely laying eyes upon her robbed him of his words again, the impact of her beauty not diminishing by the slightest even though it was already his second time seeing her like this…
Only now, the dress she wore had changed completely.

It was now as inky as the night sky, its dark surface broken by corsages of blue roses that seemed to bloom like fireworks crackling across the horizon. The obsidian fabric contrasted her pristine white skin that shimmered in the light, boldly exposed like freshly fallen snow beneath the winter sky…
Or rather, her boobs!!! More importantly, those were her boobs!!!
They’re huuuge! Gah, where did her bra even go!?

Barely forcing those thoughts right back down his throat, Masachika hurriedly reached behind himself and slammed the door shut. Yet, even as he did, he simply could not tear his eyes away from you know what: those magnificent peaks that boldly boinged outward and the alluring valley that formed between them.

No, no, calm down, Masachika. Alya’s not that busty compared to Masha-san or whatnot if we’re being objective here. It’s just her shoulders and waist are unbelievably slender that it makes her look larger than she really is. Calm down, they’re not that big if you look at it…
Still standing there frozen on the spot, Masachika continued to let his eyes wander.
Who am I kidding, they’re freaking huge. She’s, like, basically straight out of a manga or something, ain’t she?
Even after an attempt to analyze the situation as rationally as possible, the sight before him was so mind-boggling that he was at a complete loss for what to do.
Lightly tugging at the hem of her skirt, Alisa shot a teasing smirk his way as she struck a coquettish pose.
Her gleaming white leg gradually came into view… and then her left as well. A suuuper surprise.
No, seriously, where did her bra really go!?
Unable to find where their straps were supposed to be, Masachika’s ears filled with a scream he refused to let escape.

It was strange. The dress objectively covered far more than a swimsuit ever would, yet the crucial areas a normal swimsuit would have served to keep protected felt as fragile and bare as armor merely made of paper. It could only be described as an imbalance that dangled his brain on the edge of bugging out.
Alisa’s grin curved upwards even more.
【Your present is… M… E…♡】

Her dress, though dark as a moonless ocean, gleamed with a bewitching sheen as it traced along her waist as it arched sharply like a bow. It emphasized the curves brought about by her figure sharply, as if it existed solely to frame and accentuate her supreme beauty. Just catching a few glimpses of the patches of her pure white flesh it left out exposed felt illegal and so… alluringly sensual that it threatened to take Masachika’s breath away.

Such a sight, combined with the sheer devastation of her sweetly whispered woo in Russian, was more than enough to leave him beyond flushed like a rose caught beneath the summer sun. His mind simply froze.
Just how long did the two of them remain staring at each other like that?
Before she knew it, Alisa, too, glowed with a faint flush that gradually stretched from her collarbone toward her chest…

tr: Ah, içinden kan akıyor. Wooow, yani sonuçta o gerçekten yaşayan bir insan, ha?
Masachika aklının bir köşesinden geçen saçma bir yorumla uğraşırken, açık teni artık yumuşak kiraz pembesine boyanmış olan Alisa topuğunun üzerinde döndü.
“Öleceğim.”
Sesi korkutucu derecede ciddiydi, o kadar saçma değildi ki Masachika’yı resmen transtan çıkardı ve anında zıplamasına neden oldu.
“H-hey! Dur bir saniye!” hızla elini çekti ve pencereye doğru yürürken onu durdurdu. “Böyle giyinerek ölmeye gitme!”

“Böyle giyinmiş.” Belki de Alisa’nın aniden ne giydiğini fark etmesini sağlayan sözler. Çılgınca göğsünü kapatarak Masachika’ya keskin bir bakış attı, birkaç dakika öncesine göre tamamen tersine döndü.
“B-bana öyle bakma!”
“İmkansızı istiyorsun…” Masachika, son derece mantıksız bir şikayet karşısında uzun bir iç çekti.
Ya da daha doğrusu, onları doğru düzgün saklayamıyorsun bile… Ve dürüst olmak gerekirse, bunu aslında daha ero hissettirmeye çalışmak… Öhöm.
Öncelikle elbise, eğer kendini kapalı tutmakla ilgileniyorsa yan göğüs durumunu tam bir felakete dönüştürüyordu.
Yani, bu şekilde örtbas etmeye çalışsanız bile…
Bu gözlemini akıllıca kendine saklayan Masachika, parmağını şakağına bastırdı.
“Uhhh, yani…” bileğini ona doğru salladı. “Burada ne işin var?”
“Bu-el sanatları kulübü, ımm, aslında bunu… bana dayattı…”
Masachika burnunun kemerini sıktı. “Yine o kızlar…”

Ayrıntıları Alisa’dan duyan her şey, el sanatları kulübü üyelerinin, öğrenci konseyi üyelerinin Noel partisine katılacaklarını ve görünüşe göre her kadın üyeye ibadete giderken elbiselerinden birini kabul etmeleri için yalvaracaklarını duymasıyla başladı.
Yani ona bu kadar mükemmel uymasının nedeni, tüm bu karşı cins kıyafetleri giyme olayının ölçülerini daha önceden almış olmaları, değil mi?
“Ha?” Masachika parçaları bir araya getirdi. “Yani bu, Masha-san ve Sarashina-senpai’ye de ulaştıkları anlamına mı geliyor?”
“…Onlarınki orada, tamam mı?”

Alisa’nın bakışlarını takip eden Masachika, kanepeye dizilmiş dört elbise çantasını gördü. Dolu göründüklerini görmek için kısa bir bakış atması yeterliydi. Beklendiği gibi herkes kendi elbiseleriyle gitmeye karar vermişti.
Yani bu rakamlar, değil mi? Masachika, Alisa’yı baştan aşağı süzdü. Alya’nın böyle görünmesi Masha-san’ın muhtemelen daha da çılgın olacağı anlamına geliyor, yani…
“Masachika-kun mu?” Alisa buz gibi bir bakışla ona baktı.
“E-evet! Nedir bu?”
“Ben sana bana bakmayı bırakmanı söylemiştim!”
Sol elini kaldırarak yüzünü sertçe yana çevirdi ve boğazının derinliklerinden sert, istemsiz bir homurtu çıkardı.
“Vah!”
Palm hâlâ yanağını itiyordu, kız onu kapıya doğru zorladı.
İşler böyle devam ederse boynunun kırılabileceğinden korkan Masachika, onunla tekrar göz göze gelmeden başını yana çevirdi.
Alisa ancak o tökezleyerek uzaklaştıktan sonra nihayet elini geri çekebildi.
“Ben-ben de bunu benim için yaptıkları için deneyeceğimi düşündüm, ama… Tanrım! Tam da düşündüğüm gibi, eski halime dönüyorum! Eski halime dönüyorum, o yüzden defol!”
“…Tamam.”
Alisa’nın biçimde bir mazeret sunacak sabrı olmasıyla Masachika, kalbinin ona hafifçe geri dönmesi için baskı yapmasına rağmen odadan çıktı.
Şimdi sırtı dışarıdaki kapıya dönük dururken uzun, derin bir iç çekti.
Yani, bir yolunu bulup… Alya’nın hala Alya olması beni rahatlattı sanırım…

Alisa’nın kapanış töreni sırasında omuzlarını tutma şekli zaten bir öğrenci konseyi başkanının tavrını akla getiriyordu. Ve birkaç dakika önce onun önünde duruşu vardı; o kadar nefes kesici derecede güzeldi ki, saf bir zarafetle giyinmişti, çekiciliğini sadece kelimelerle anlatmak aşağılayıcı geliyordu. Ona her iki şekilde de tanık olmak, Masachika’nın biçimde onun ulaşamayacağı bir yere taşınmış gibi hissetmesine neden olmuştu…
Ama sonuçta görünüşe göre hiç de öyle olmamıştı.
Hayır, ama… belki de bu sadece bir zaman meselesidir.

Alisa’nın gözlerindeki canlılık, birkaç saat önce onun konuşmasını sahnenin kenarından izlediğini yeniden yaşarken zihninde parladı. Kendi tanıtımından sonra seyircinin mutlak sınırına kadar zorlanan beklentileriyle karşı karşıya kaldığı için muazzam bir baskı altında kalmıştı.
Ama yine de, böylesine bir spot ışığı altında gözleri kör olmuşken bile, sonuna kadar ideallerinden cesurca bahsetmiş, en ufak bir tereddüt dahi göstermemişti.
Benim… kahretsin, Yuki’nin bile… böyle bir şeyi başarmış olmasının imkânı yok.
Bu, Masachika’nın gerçekten yemin ettiği bir kanaatti. Şu anda emin olduğu tek şey buydu: asla onunla boy ölçüşemezdi.
Bunu itiraf etmek zorundaydı. Alisa’nın büyüme hızı ve ilerleme hızı onun hayal edebileceği her şeyin çok ötesine geçmişti. Bu hiç şüphesiz kendisininkinden bile daha hızlıydı.

Onun yanında daha ne kadar kalabileceğini sorabilirsiniz? Deneyim, bağlantılar, iletişim, bunların hepsi Masachika’nın biraz üstün olduğu şeylerdi. Onu destekleyebilecek biri olarak neden hala ona ihtiyaç duyduğunun nedenleri bunlardı.
Ancak… yavaş yavaş Alisa artık ona bunun için bile ihtiyaç duymadığı bir noktaya ulaşıyordu. Bugünkü kapanış töreninin açıkça ortaya koyduğu şey de buydu.
Pekala, yapabileceğim tek şey dayanmaya devam etmek, değil mi? Masachika düşüncelerini kesiyormuş gibi kendine güven verdi.

Zaten kendi yetersizliklerine kafa yormayı bırakmaya karar vermişti, bunların üzerinde durmanın onu yalnızca ayakta tuttuğunu fark etmişti. Bu onun sonunda geride kalacağı günün geleceği anlamına gelse bile…
Çünkü o zamana kadar yapabileceği tek şey, sahip olduğu her şeyle onun ayak izlerini takip etmeye devam etmekti. Sonuçları ne olursa olsun.
Clack. Kapı arkasından açılırken mandalın açılma sesi Masachika’nın sarsılmasına neden oldu.
“…Sizi beklettiğim için üzgünüm,” diye baktı Alisa.
“…Evet.”
Orijinal gece elbisesine geri dönmüştü, beceriksizce onun bakışlarıyla buluşmayı başaramadığı için kıpırdanıyordu…
Midesindeki düğüm nihayet çözülürken, yerini sessiz bir hayal kırıklığı acısı çeken Masachika bir kez daha ona kolunu uzattı.
“Peki o zaman gidelim mi?”
“…Evet.”
Başını sallayan Alisa sonunda kolunu düzgünce onun etrafına doladı. İkisi yavaş yavaş yürümeye başladılar.

Koridorda vals yapıp merdivenlerden indiler, koridorun sonundaki kapıdan çıkıp partinin yapıldığı spor salonuna doğru ilerlediler. Resmi olarak başlamasına henüz biraz zaman olsa da, mekandan taşan canlı atmosfer, şimdiden oldukça büyük bir kalabalığın toplandığını gösteriyordu.
Uzaktan sahneyi içine çeken Masachika, farkına bile varmadan kendini olduğu yerde buldu…
“Hım?” Alisa gözlerini ona doğru kaydırdı. “Sorun nedir?”
“…Hiçbir şey.”

Reddi neredeyse refleks olarak geldi ama nedeni açıktı. Tanıdık kendini küçümseme duygusu: Yanındaki kızla içeri girerken etraflarındaki gözleri üzerine çekmek üzere olduklarını anlayınca bir kez daha dişlerini diken bir aşağılık kompleksi.
Ortağı olarak onun yanında olmaya layık değilim.
Nasıl bakarsanız bakın, biz kesinlikle uyuşmuyoruz.
Onu olduğu yerde sabit tutan düşünceler bunlardı.
Hayır, yani… bunu sadece bize bakarak anlıyoruz, değil mi? Haaah, böyle zamanlar gerçekten keşke hala o yenilmez modda olabilseydim.
Ona, sallayamadığı bir lanet gibi yapışan alaycılığın tamamen farkında olmayan Alisa -ona endişe ve endişe karışımı karışık bir bakışla bakıyordu- ona muzip bir gülümsemeyle karşılık verdi.
“Olabilir mi… beni elbisemin içinde kimseye göstermek istemedin?”
Kendisiyle o kadar dolu bir soruydu ki, başka birinden gelseydi gülüp geçmek kolay olurdu.
Masachika yalnızca alaycı, çaresiz bir gülümseme sunabildi. “…Evet sanırım öyle. Sanırım o kadar güzelsin ki seni kendime saklamaktan kendimi alamıyorum Alya.”
Alisa geriye doğru sıçradı, tüm vücudu ani şokla gerildi.
“…Gerçekten mi?” diye ciyakladı, kendini çok geç fark etti. “Eh… sanırım umurumda değil… eğer durum buysa? Ama yine de…”

Sözlerini bitiremeyen Masachika, utancını gizlemek için saçını geriye doğru taradı, bu arada Masachika yalnızca kaşlarını çatabildi, sözlerinin nereye vardığını bulmaya çalışırken ifadesi kafa karışıklığıyla gölgelendi.
Ona doğru birkaç yan bakış atan Alisa tekrar konuştu.

“Eğer istediğin, kültür festivalinin sonraki partisinde olduğu gibi, birlikte yalnız dans etmekse… o zaman bu da benim için sorun değil, biliyorsun değil mi? Ne de olsa eşlik edilen benim. Ben de sana eşlik edeceğim.”
O kadar cesurca ifade ettiği sözleri, onun mutlak güvenini ve doğrudan onun kollarına düşme isteğini yansıtıyordu… Masachika’nın kalbine diken diken olan tüm aşağılık duygusunu anında yok etti.
Evet, haklı, değil mi? Eğer böyle bir şey söylüyorsa, bu aptal aşağılık kompleksinin bana eziyet etmesini kaldıramam. Burada başımı dik tutamazsam gerçekten erkek değilim, değil mi?
Damarlarında her şeye gücü yeten bir dalganın aktığını hisseden Masachika, yenilmez modunun bir kez daha yeniden etkinleştiğini hissetti.
“Bana bu kadar güvendiğin için teşekkür ederim,” diye korkusuzca gülümsedi. “…Ama dürüst olmak gerekirse şu anda seni herkese göstermek istiyorum.”
“Aman Tanrım, öyle mi?” Alisa’nın dudakları kışkırtıcı bir sırıtışla kıvrıldı. “O halde başımızı dik tutalım ve herkese bakacak bir şeyler verelim, olur mu?”
Sesindeki katıksız küstahlık bile gülünçtü. Masachika sadece kıkırdayarak ellerini yenilgiyle havaya kaldırdı.
“Tamam gidelim mi prensesim?”
“Evet. Hadi gidelim olur mu?”
en: Ah, she’s got blood flowing through her. Wooow, so she really is a living human after all, huuuh?
While Masachika coped with an absurd comment that drifted through a corner of his mind, Alisa—her fair skin now stained a soft cherry pink—spun around on her heel.
“I’m going to die.”
Her tone was frighteningly serious, so no-nonsense that it practically punched Masachika right out of his trance, making him jump right on the spot.
“H-hey! Wait a sec!” he quickly yanked her hand, stopping her as she started toward the window. “Don’t go dyin’ dressed like that!!!”

“Dressed like that.” Words that perhaps made Alisa suddenly aware of what she was wearing. Frantically covering her chest, she shot a sharp glare Masachika’s way, a complete reversal from just moments ago.
“D-don’t stare at me like that!”
“You’re asking the impossible…” Masachika let out a long sigh to what was quite simply an utterly unreasonable complaint.
Or rather, you’re not even really hiding them properly anyway… And honestly, trying to actually makes it feel more ero… Ahem.
To begin with, the dress made her side-boob situation basically a complete disaster if she was concerned with keeping herself covered.
So, like, even if you try to cover it like that…
Wisely keeping that observation to himself, Masachika pressed a finger to his temple.
“Uhhh, so…” he flicked his wrist toward her. “What’s the whole deal with this here?”
“Th-the handicrafts club, um, basically forced it… on me…”
Masachika pinched the bridge of his nose. “Those girls again…”

Hearing the details from Alisa, it all began once the members of the handicrafts club had heard that the members of the student council would be attending the Christmas party, apparently pleading every female member to accept one of their dresses to the point of worship.
So the reason why it fits her so perfectly is ’cause they’d already gotten her measurements for that whole crossdressing thing earlier, huh?
“Huh?” Masachika put the pieces together. “So that means they got to Masha-san and Sarashina-senpai too?”
“…Theirs are there, okay?”

Following Alisa’s gaze, Masachika spotted four garment bags lined up on the sofa. He only needed a quick glance to see that they looked full. As expected, everyone else had decided to go with their own dresses.
I mean, that figures, yeah? Masachika looked Alisa up and down. Alya’s one looking like this means Masha-san’s would’ve probably been even more insane, so…
“Masachika-kun?” Alisa fixed him with an icy stare.
“Y-yes! What is it?”
“I-I told you to quit staring at me!”
Raising her left hand, she firmly swatted his face to the side, drawing a harsh, involuntary grunt from deep in his throat.
“Guh!”
Palm still pushed on his cheek, she forced him toward the door.
Fearing his neck might snap if things continued like this, Masachika whipped his head to the side before he could meet her eyes again.
Only after he stumbled away did Alisa finally pull her hand back.
“I-I figured I’d try it on since they made it for me, but… Geez! As I thought, I’m changing back! I’m changing back, so get out!”
“…Okaaay.”
With Alisa somehow having the patience to provide an excuse, Masachika left the room in spite of his heart lightly tugging at him to turn back.
Now standing with his back against the door outside, he let out a long, deep sigh.
I mean, I’m somehow… relieved that Alya’s still Alya, I guess…

The way Alisa held her shoulders during the closing ceremony had already suggested the bearing of a student council president. And then there was the way she stood in front of him just moments ago, so breathtakingly beautiful and draped in pure elegance that using just words to describe her charm felt insulting. Witnessing her in both of those ways had made Masachika feel as though she had somehow moved to a place far beyond his reach…
Yet in the end, it had apparently never been like that at all.
No, but… maybe it’s only a matter of time.

The vigor in Alisa’s eyes flashed across his mind as he relived watching her speech from the wings of the stage just a few hours earlier. She had been pressed by an immense pressure, facing the expectations of the audience that had been pushed to its absolute limit after his own introduction. And yet, even when blinded under such a spotlight, she had spoken of her ideals boldly, not hinting at even the slightest bit of hesitation all the way to the end.
There’s no way I… hell, not even Yuki… could’ve pulled something like that.
It was a conviction that Masachika genuinely swore by. It was all he was sure about at this moment: he could never measure up to her.
